task.description: WF-03 Step 2: produce the fix design for ISS-0780 (design only, no implementation) covering the corrected @allow_headers value, the stale moduledoc comment, the pinned test assertion that needs to change, and the shape of the new regression test for TEST-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: corrected @allow_headers value stated exactly, with ordering convention justified
moduledoc comment (lines 66-68) rewritten to match the five-header reality
the pinned assertion in cors_test.exs (~line 187-188) has its required new value stated exactly
the shape of a new ISS-0780 regression test is specified, with an explicit recommendation on single-exemplar-header vs. all-three coverage and a justification
no implementation code (no .ex/.exs code fences with real function bodies)

result.summary:
PRECEDENT CHECK (per task instruction, before designing): grepped lib/letflow/design/ for a CORS-fix precedent. ISS-0777 (BLOCKER, two-tier identifier-validation logic spanning two modules with real branching behavior) has a full design doc (iss0777-entity-type-identifier-validation.md) -- proportionate to its actual logic complexity. ISS-0529 (MAJOR, the closest precedent -- also an additive change to lib/letflow/plugs/cors.ex's constants, also fixed by adding entries to an allowlist plus new cors_test.exs regression tests) has NO file under lib/letflow/design/ at all; its design was carried inline through the WF-03 run rather than as a standalone artefact. ISS-0780 is strictly smaller in scope than ISS-0529 (a single string constant edit plus a comment, versus ISS-0529's array-of-origins change with real per-origin match logic via origin_allowed?/1) and involves zero new branching logic or new module. Following the ISS-0529 precedent: no separate lib/letflow/design/ file created. Design recorded here instead, matching the established level of ceremony for a change this size.

1) CORRECTED @allow_headers (lib/letflow/plugs/cors.ex line 69):

   @allow_headers "authorization, content-type, idempotency-key, if-match, x-bpm-user-id"

   Ordering: plain alphabetical (a, c, i-d, i-f, x), which is also what the existing two-header value already happens to be (authorization before content-type). Alphabetical is a deterministic, drift-resistant convention -- the next header added later has one unambiguous place to go, and a diff reviewer can verify placement without needing project-specific knowledge of arrival order or perceived importance. Case: keeps the existing all-lowercase style (the current value is already lowercase; HTTP header names are case-insensitive and this file's own moduledoc explicitly established lowercase as the convention). Separator: keeps the existing ', ' (comma-space) join, single string, not a list -- no other part of the module treats @allow_headers as anything but an opaque string written straight into put_resp_header/3, so there is no reason to change its type.

2) MODULEDOC COMMENT (lines 66-68) -- replace:

   "# The two request headers the SPA actually sends (`client.ts`): the bearer
   # token and the JSON content type. Deliberately an explicit allowlist, not
   # an echo of the request's `access-control-request-headers` value."

   with (content/wording is CODE-DESIGNER's design intent; ELIXIR-DEV renders the exact comment text verbatim, this is not implementation code, it is comment prose):

   "# The five request headers the SPA actually sends across web/src/api/*.ts:
   # `authorization` and `content-type` (client.ts, every request),
   # `x-bpm-user-id` (client.ts, every authenticated request -- extracted
   # from the JWT `sub` claim), `if-match` (entities.ts, optimistic-
   # concurrency PUT, REQ-336), and `idempotency-key` (onboarding.ts,
   # POST /api/v1/onboarding). Deliberately an explicit allowlist, not an
   # echo of the request's `access-control-request-headers` value. Audited
   # against the full web/src tree (ISS-0780) -- this is the complete set;
   # keep it that way rather than letting it drift again."

   Rationale for the added closing sentence: the diagnosis (step-01) found this exact drift -- the old comment claimed 'the two' headers and was never updated when x-bpm-user-id/if-match/idempotency-key were added over time -- so the replacement comment should make the audit-completeness claim and its date/issue-id explicit, the same way @default_origins' own comment already cites ISS-0529 inline as a permanent anti-drift marker. This is stylistically consistent with the existing file, not a new convention.

3) TEST ASSERTION CHANGE -- test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs ~line 187-188, inside 'AC3: preflight OPTIONS request, matched origin' > 'gets 204 with the full preflight header set...'. Current (characterizes the bug verbatim):

   assert get_resp_header(conn, "access-control-allow-headers") ==
            ["authorization, content-type"]

   Required new value (exact string, must match the corrected @allow_headers byte-for-byte since this assertion does full-string equality, not substring/membership):

   assert get_resp_header(conn, "access-control-allow-headers") ==
            ["authorization, content-type, idempotency-key, if-match, x-bpm-user-id"]

   No other part of this test (status 204, resp_body, allow-origin, vary, allow-methods, max-age assertions in the same test) needs to change -- only this one assertion's literal.

4) NEW REGRESSION TEST SHAPE (for TEST-DESIGNER, Step 4) -- RECOMMENDATION: one new test covering all three added headers together in a single OPTIONS preflight, not three separate single-header tests. Place it in the same 'AC3: preflight OPTIONS request, matched origin' describe block, immediately after the test touched in (3), named to name the issue (e.g. 'ISS-0780 regression: x-bpm-user-id, if-match, and idempotency-key are all allowed on preflight').

   Shape: an OPTIONS request to /api/v1/anything, same as the existing AC3 test, with headers:
     - origin: @allowed_origin
     - access-control-request-method: "POST"
     - access-control-request-headers: "x-bpm-user-id, if-match, idempotency-key"
           (fix_direction's literal exemplar, x-bpm-user-id, is the first token -- included verbatim, not paraphrased -- with the other two audited headers alongside it in the same request, since they share the exact same code path and were found by the same audit)
   Assert: conn.status == 204, and that access-control-allow-headers's single response value contains all three added header names -- expressed as a membership/substring check (e.g. splitting the response header string on ', ' and asserting ["x-bpm-user-id", "if-match", "idempotency-key"] are each present in that split list), NOT a full-string equality against the corrected @allow_headers value, so this test's intent (these three specific headers are present) stays legible independently of assertion (3)'s exact-string pin.

   JUSTIFICATION for one combined test over three single-header tests (per the task's request to decide and justify briefly): unlike ISS-0529's two origin tests -- which existed because @default_origins is matched through real per-origin branching logic (origin_allowed?/1, an Enum membership check with actual conditional behavior per distinct origin) where each origin is a genuinely separate code path worth separately exercising -- @allow_headers has no branching at all: it is a single static string written unconditionally into one response header on every matched-origin preflight. There is exactly one code path, so three separate tests would only assert the same static string three different ways -- duplicated ceremony with no additional path coverage. One combined test that literally reproduces fix_direction's request-header set in a single preflight is proportionate: it demonstrates the real-world case (a client that needs more than one of these headers on one request, as entities.ts and onboarding.ts callers actually do at different times) and gives true fail-then-pass regression evidence for the full fix scope in one assertion block. Assertion (3)'s corrected full-string pin already provides exact-value regression coverage as a byproduct of un-characterizing the bug, so the new test's job is specifically to prove the issue's literal reproduction case (a preflight requesting these headers) now succeeds -- redundant three-way duplication would not add coverage assertion (3) doesn't already give.

No implementation code was written -- all of the above are exact literal values/comment text to be placed into existing lines by ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER, not function bodies, case/cond logic, or module structure changes; the module's existing control flow (handle_allowed/2, preflight_request?/1, etc.) is untouched by this fix.
issues: No separate lib/letflow/design/ file was created for this fix, per the ISS-0529 precedent check documented above -- flagging for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR in case it disagrees with that ceremony-level call for this specific case size.
